ideas.title: Winch the empty cart up the planks (project winch, next step)
ideas.critique: Finally the motor does work against a load the player built, and rope, rolling contact, mesh-volume mass and a motor torque coupled every step, with stall-or-climb decided by pulleys and grease, is the first real machine on the road. The risk is that it shrinks to a winch that always pulls the same cart up one fixed slope, which plays once; and the film has to show the rope actually going taut, not a cart sliding along a rail.

ideas.title: Hear the load: the commutator's crackle comes from the circuit
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Sound made from the circuit's own break energies and commutation rate is new for the island, and hearing a stall coming is a real skill to learn. But the arc spectrum (hiss vs snap) is a mapping you choose, not something solved, and on its own it is only something to listen to until the winch gives the ear a decision to make.

ideas.title: Lumi turns the brush rocker by hand (project brushes)
ideas.critique: Per-coil branches, contact overlap and armature reaction shifting the neutral with load are real commutation physics, and Lumi's hand really holding a part is overdue. Without a load the sweet spot never moves, so this hangs on the winch: alone it is one more glance at the same sparks, with the IK as the only new thing to watch.

ideas.title: Crank the drum backwards: the dynamo lights a wire
ideas.critique: Making a generator from the same Motor.step! is a true road step, and a crank whose drag grows with the current is a good thing to feel. The payoff, though, is the same wire glowing and parting that 'Where I rushed it' already showed, and the human's goals name the very example 'a generator that lights a wire', so it will read as expected.

ideas.title: Form the lead plates: an accumulator you have to train
ideas.critique: Planté forming, where capacity grows with each cycle and the battery remembers how you trained it, is an unusual mechanic with depth, and the store is the core the cart is missing. The electrochemistry is easily a fitted curve per cycle, and it needs a cranked dynamo that does not exist yet, so the first session may be fizz in a jar with nothing to charge it.

ideas.title: Three ponies on the cart: weight from what they are
ideas.critique: Mass from mesh volume is honest, and the friend stepping off by mood is a cute gag, but the payoff is the friends' reaction and the stall is just the winch's stall torque compared with a sum. It is a premature lap of the big goal's moment, before there is a cart that drives.

ideas.title: The eddy brake: a copper disc that slows the cart and fills the plates
ideas.critique: Eddy currents from the field solver are fresh physics, and braking without contact surprises people. But there is no cart rolling down a dune and no plates to charge, so for now it is a disc slowing on a bench, and the 2D solver will hold only for one disc in one gap.

ideas.title: Pitted copper: the commutator wears and Lumi files it smooth
ideas.critique: Wear that lasts across sessions, drawn from a per-segment map, is a nice material idea, and a macro still could look good. But erosion per joule is one number you choose, and a chore of filing is upkeep, not play; it polishes a part before the machine has done any work.

ideas.title: Reef the windmill: sail area against the gust
ideas.critique: A daily decision against the weather, where too much sail snaps a spar, answers the critic's worry about what the player does each day. It jumps ahead of the generator and the plates, though, and a blade element model plus one spar's stress limit will likely be a fitted rig unless the snapping comes out of the wood itself.

ideas.title: A volt-tongue: Lumi tastes the battery
ideas.critique: Licking the battery is a good nerdy joke, but it is really a gauge with three reactions picked from thresholds on a single current, and the payoff is Lumi's face. It reads a battery the island does not have yet.
